Senses.Explanation: 僧出 is the ordinary sequence 'a monk comes out' rather than a special doctrinal label. Baiyan Fu's compilation narrates that one monk came forward and spoke; Jiqi's record likewise says that a robed monk came out from the assembly. Xuedou Chongxian asks whether the world's monks can get out of an old woman's trap. In Huangbo Xiyun's record, the wording occurs in direct address: Huangbo calls, 'The monk who searched for the antelope yesterday, come out,' and the monk then steps forward. The sentence controls tense, direction, and whether 僧 is the subject or the person being addressed.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J37/J37nB386.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Yuan’an Feng. The line describes ordinary precedence: monastics are ordered by completed summer retreats, laypeople by seniority in years. During a rite honoring the names of myriad Buddhas, Yuan'an Liao raises a scholar's question to Changsha: where do the Buddhas named in scripture live, and do they still teach beings? Changsha responds through the already famous poem on Yellow Crane Tower, telling the scholar to compose one himself. Yuan'an proposes overturning the seat, but for the present question about the Buddhas' dwelling he would bow in greeting and give the ranking line. The reply turns the imagined search for another land toward a present act of respectful recognition rather than supplying a heavenly address.

Occurrences.Kwic: 南嶽峰頭月，清照瀟湘萬頃中。葉縣省禪師因僧問：「如何是毘盧師法身主？」師云：「僧排夏臘，俗列耆年。」進云：「向上還有事也無？」師云：「有。」僧云：「如何是向上事？」師云：「萬里崖州君自去，臨行惆悵怨他誰？」師拈云：「大小葉縣不合向奴兒婢子邊鼓弄，致有向上向下，令者僧前不遘村、後不迭店。神鼎則不然，如何是毘盧師法身主？但云：『屋北鹿獨宿。』『如何是向上事？』『溪西雞齊啼。』」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J37/J37nB388.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Yikui of Shending. Yikui Yuankui quotes Shexian Guisheng answering a question about the master of Vairocana with this ranking line. Asked whether there is anything further upward, Shexian says yes and sends the questioner toward distant Yazhou, asking whom he will blame when departing sadly. Yikui criticizes the creation of an above and below that strands the monk between places. He substitutes paired images of a deer sleeping alone north of the house and chickens crowing together west of the stream. Shexian owns the exact quoted answer; Yikui's present comment challenges its handling, so the line is not simply endorsed as an exhaustive spiritual hierarchy.

Occurrences.Kwic: 際亭李居士生日，請上堂。問：「十方同聚會，個個學無為，此是選佛場，心空及第歸。如何是十方同聚會？」師云：「僧排夏臘，俗列耆年。」進云：「如何是個個學無為？」師云：「運水底運水，搬柴底搬柴。」進云：「此是選佛場，未審選誰作佛？」師云：「唱名即不到。」進云：「如何是心空及第歸底事？」師云：「你秖好隨眾三碗兩碗。」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J38/J38nB428.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Mixingren. At an address for a layman's birthday, Mixing Jiren is asked to explain the verse about people gathering from ten directions to learn the unconditioned way. To the gathering clause he replies with monastic retreat-seniority and lay age. To learning he answers that those carrying water carry water and those hauling firewood haul firewood. Asked whom this field selects as Buddha, he says calling the name fails to reach it; the final question earns only permission to join the others for two or three bowls. The ranking line places the assembly in its actual communal order, while the successive replies return its lofty description to daily work and eating.

Linquan Conglun discusses Lingyun's realization on seeing peach blossoms and Xuansha's refusal to accept it as complete. He depicts Xuansha raising with one hand and pressing with the other, while Lingyun, accustomed to the contest, seems to yield and then asks whether his senior brother has himself penetrated the matter. Linquan compares this with Fanzhi wearing his socks inside out: others call it wrong, but he would rather offend their eyes than make his own feet suffer. The original first-person pair is the sock wearer's poetic voice, identified as Wang Fanzhi's poem by the parallel source, while Linquan is the present comparer. The foot verb is read here as discomfort or chafing, fitting the sock scene. Linquan applies the refusal to submit one's lived footing to an observer's judgment to Lingyun's returning challenge; he does not merely pronounce one teacher the winner. His following examples and closing warning ask listeners to grasp the matter before waiting becomes futile.

Huihong's Forest Notes recounts Huanglong Huinan offering a monk all the teaching in one sentence, then directing him to step to one side. When the monk moves, he is rebuked for pursuing sound and form. A second monk, having heard of this, refuses to move and is rebuked for not listening. Huihong criticizes those who reduce such teaching to straightforward verbal discussion, then says that he loves Wang Fanzhi's inside-out-socks poem and gives the exact eyes-and-feet pair. He places it beside Hanshan's poem about a person making thousand-year plans and an iron threshold while ghosts laugh, and says that a practitioner should look at his own conduct and the world in such a playful way. Here the old poem supports a present stance toward appearances, judgment and worldly planning. Wang Fanzhi remains the non-Zen poet's voice; Huihong is the current author applying it. The poem's secular origin is not counted as a third Zen use, and the local sock contrast governs the reading of the foot's discomfort.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X78/X78n1554.xml). Praise of the Orthodox Lineage of the Five Houses. Qingyuan sends Shitou Xiqian to Nanyue Huairang with a letter and promises him an adze for living on a mountain when he returns. Before presenting the letter, Shitou asks what it is like not to seek the holy ones or esteem one's own inner spirit. Huairang calls the question too lofty and asks why he does not ask lower. Shitou answers that he would rather sink for endless ages than seek release from the holy ones. He returns to Qingyuan without delivering either letter or message and asks for the promised adze; Qingyuan lowers one foot, and Shitou bows. The exact defiant pair belongs to Shitou, not Huairang. Senses.Explanation: Better to sink for endless ages than seek release from the holy ones. Qingyuan sends Shitou Xiqian to Nanyue Huairang with a letter and promises him an adze for living on a mountain when he returns. Before presenting the letter, Shitou asks what it is like not to seek the holy ones or esteem one's own inner spirit. Huairang calls the question too lofty and asks why he does not ask lower. Occurrences.Kwic: 中釘橛，靈虗旱地遭釘。雪竇不管盡法無民，只要話行千古。檢點將來，總是一隊掠虗漢。舉：夾山與定山同行，言話次，定云：生死中無佛，則無生死。夾云：生死中有佛，則不迷生死。互相不肯，同上大梅。相見了，具說前事，梅云：一親一疎。夾問：那箇親？那箇疎？梅云：且去，明日來。夾至來日，又問：未審那箇親？梅云：親者不問，問者不親。夾山住後云：我當時在。大梅失却一隻眼。雪竇云：夾山畢竟不知換得一隻眼。大梅老漢當時聞舉，若以棒一時打出，豈止畫斷兩人葛藤，亦乃天下宗匠。師云：夾山失却隻眼，住後方知；雪竇畫斷葛藤，作得天下宗匠。雖然，李將軍有佳聲在，不得封侯也是閑。舉：僧問保福：雪峯平生有何言句，得似羚羊掛角時？福云：我不可作雪峯弟子不得。雪竇云：一千五百箇布衲。保福較些子。師云：做得雪峯弟子則不無，要見羚羊掛角，三生六十劫。舉，僧問長慶：羚羊未掛角時如何？慶云：草裡漢。僧云：掛角後如何？慶云：亂叫喚。僧云：畢竟如何？慶云：驢事未去，馬事到來。雪竇云：寧可碎身如微塵，終不瞎箇眾生眼。長慶較些子，復云：一般漢，設使羚羊未掛角，也似萬里望鄉關。師云：長慶恁麼答話，瞎却天下人眼去在。雪竇道：終不瞎箇眾生眼，萬里望鄉關。舉，僧問巴陵：祖意教意，是同是別？陵云：雞寒上樹，鴨寒下水。僧問睦州：祖意教意，是同是別？州云：青山自青山，白雲自白雲。雪竇云：問既一般，答亦相似，其中有利他自利，瞞人自瞞，若點撿分明，管取解空第一。師云：雞寒上樹，鴨寒下水，青山嵯峨，白雲澹泞，祖意教意在什麼處？若約撿點分明，有利無利不離行市。舉趙州示眾云：今夜答話去也，有解問者出來。時有僧出，州云：比擬拋塼引玉，引得箇墼子。法眼遂乃舉問覺鐵觜：先師意作麼生？覺云：如國家拜將。乃問：甚人去得？時有人出云：某甲去得。須云：汝去不得。法眼云：我會也。雪竇云：靈利漢聞舉，便知落處。然雖如是，放過覺鐵觜。夫宗師語不虗發，出來必是作家，因什麼拋塼引墼？諸禪德要識趙州麼？從前汗馬無人識，只要重論蓋代功。師云：覺鐵觜名喧宇宙，拶著便作屎臭氣。人問：拋塼引墼，便謂如國家拜將。當時法眼若解拈出本分草料，何止清風萬里？雪竇云：靈利漢一舉便知落處，豈堪共語？然雖如是，放過覺鐵觜，賴有此語。舉：耽源辭國師歸省馬祖，於地上作一圓相，展坐具禮拜。祖云：你欲作佛去。源云：
